text.en: Several owners praise trainers like DJ and Chyna for their patience, clear guidance, and hands-on help during group sessions. In contrast, negative reviews mention insufficient supervision during puppy play and a perceived lack of individual support for owners.

Many puppy owners report strong results in foundational socialization, good manners, and handler coordination through weekly themed classes. However, dissatisfied clients felt the training lacked clear structure and failed to deliver noticeable behavioral gains.

Clients appreciate structured play sessions where young dogs burn energy and practice appropriate dog-to-dog etiquette with peers. Nonetheless, one reviewer reported that dominant puppies overwhelmed timid ones without prompt intervention from attending staff.

q.en: How are group puppy classes structured?

a.en: Reviews note that classes typically feature 2 to 3 trainers, combining structured obedience exercises with supervised puppy play.

q.en: What concerns have been raised regarding group play?

a.en: One client felt staff intervened too slowly when larger or more dominant puppies overwhelmed more timid participants.

q.en: Do trainers provide hands-on help for new pet parents?

a.en: Yes, several reviewers emphasize that instructors show great patience helping first-time owners practice handling mechanics.

q.en: Can puppies transition into more advanced classes?

a.en: Clients mention progressing smoothly from puppy kindergarten into adult obedience courses and specialty workshops.
